blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: This file runs a Pod meant for a node reserved for databases. It comes from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: A taint on a node keeps ordinary Pods off it. Only Pods that tolerate the taint may run there.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Pod, from the core v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name to see which node it landed on.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Pod
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: db-pod

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: A busybox container that sleeps stands in for a database. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: A real database image is large. The lesson is about where the Pod runs, not what it runs.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without containers, Kubernetes rejects the Pod.
blocks.comment: A stand-in for a database: a container that sleeps
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: db-pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: db
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Go to database nodes
blocks.what: nodeSelector sends the Pod only to nodes labelled role=db.
blocks.why: A toleration only lets a Pod onto a tainted node. The label is what draws it there.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Pod can land on any node it tolerates, including ordinary ones.
blocks.comment: Run only on nodes labelled role=db
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: db-pod
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    role: db
  containers:
    - name: db
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Tolerate the taint
blocks.what: The toleration matches the taint role=db with effect NoSchedule.
blocks.why: Without it, the taint would keep this Pod off the database node too.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Pod waits in Pending: the only role=db node has a taint it does not tolerate.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: db-pod
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    role: db
  tolerations:
    - key: role
      operator: Equal
      value: db
      effect: NoSchedule
  containers:
    - name: db
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Pods are in the core v1 API.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Pod runs one or more containers together.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Pod’s name. kubectl get pod db-pod -o wide shows its node.
notes.spec: The desired state: what to run, and where.
notes.spec.nodeSelector: Node labels the Pod requires. A simpler form of node affinity.
notes.spec.tolerations: Taints this Pod accepts. Each list item matches one taint.
notes.spec.tolerations[].operator: Equal: the taint’s value must match value below. Exists matches any value.
notes.spec.tolerations[].effect: NoSchedule: the taint blocks new Pods that do not tolerate it.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.containers[].command: Sleep for an hour, standing in for a database.

tryIt.result: Lists the three nodes. Pick one name to reserve for databases.
Labels the node, so the Pod’s nodeSelector can find it.

check.run: kubectl label node $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') role=db

tryIt.result: Prints node/<node> tainted. New Pods without a matching toleration now avoid it.

check.run: kubectl taint node $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') role=db:NoSchedule

tryIt.result: db-pod is Running on the node you tainted.
Starts four ordinary Pods, with no toleration.
None of the four Pods is on the tainted node.

check.run: kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/others --timeout=90s >/dev/null && kubectl get pods -l app=others --field-selector spec.nodeName=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -o name

tryIt.result: Removes db-pod. It takes up to 30 seconds, because sleep ignores the stop signal.
The dash removes the taint. Prints node/<node> untainted.

check.run: kubectl taint node $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') role=db:NoSchedule-

tryIt.result: Removes the label. Prints node/<node> unlabeled.

check.run: kubectl label node $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') role-

questions.question: Does the toleration on its own send db-pod to the database node?
answers: Yes, a toleration attracts the Pod
No, it only allows it. nodeSelector sends it there.
Only if the node has no label
questions.explain: A toleration removes a barrier. The nodeSelector is what points the Pod at the node.

questions.question: An ordinary Pod without this toleration is created. Where can it run?
answers: On any node except the tainted one
questions.explain: NoSchedule keeps new Pods off the tainted node unless they tolerate it.

questions.question: Which effect would also remove Pods already running on the node?
questions.explain: NoExecute evicts running Pods that do not tolerate it. NoSchedule only affects new Pods.

fix.message: The Pod "db-pod" is invalid: spec.tolerations[0].effect: Unsupported value: "NoSchedul": supported values: "NoSchedule", "PreferNoSchedule", "NoExecute"
fix.explain: Kubernetes knows three effects. NoSchedul is a typo, so the toleration means nothing.
fix.fix: Spell the effect in full: NoSchedule.
